title: Why Does Salt Melt Ice?
description:
Salt melts ice, but how? At 0 °C, ice and water trade molecules at the same rate, so nothing seems to change. Dissolved salt ions crowd the water next to the ice, so fewer water molecules stick, while melting goes on at nearly the same rate: the ice shrinks. Melting takes heat, so salty ice water cools itself below zero, down toward about −21 °C with enough table salt. That is how ice cream in a bag works, why road salt gets too slow below about −9 °C, and how a pinch of salt lets you lift an ice cube with a thread.
